articles.headline: datasette-auth-github 1.0 lands on GitHub – OAuth for Datasette 0.65
articles.dek: The new plugin adds first‑class GitHub OAuth to Datasette 0.65 and tightens cookie handling for Mobile Safari.

body.text: Key Takeaway

Version 1.0 of datasette‑auth‑github ships on GitHub, wiring GitHub sign‑in directly into Datasette 0.65 and fixing a Safari cookie bug that previously broke login flows. Builders can drop the plugin into any existing Datasette deployment and get secure auth without extra server code. [FACT:95b9f89a81becbb5db4a298c4b9c1042][FACT:b8b12bf3e952d00649e4fdc7a8767626]
Why This Matters

Authentication is a constant friction point for data‑driven apps. By delegating to GitHub, you inherit OAuth best practices and avoid rolling your own token store. The plugin also respects Mobile Safari's stricter cookie policy, so your users on iOS won’t be bounced back to a login screen. That translates to faster onboarding and fewer support tickets. [FACT:d498f760197187160cd51ea3de3b6be2][FACT:b8b12bf3e952d00649e4fdc7a8767626]
What Happened

Simon Willison announced the release on Sep 19 2026. The GitHub repo now carries a v1.0 tag and includes the updated Python package that targets Datasette 0.65+. The release notes call out three changes: GitHub OAuth flow, a fix for Safari’s SameSite cookie handling, and updated plugin metadata for easier discovery. [FACT:95b9f89a81becbb5db4a298c4b9c1042][FACT:c54a37e27696caa08553e2659c8c99d4]
Builder View

To adopt the plugin, add `datasette-auth-github==1.0` to your environment, register a GitHub OAuth app, and point `metadata.json` at the new auth URL. No code changes are required beyond the config file. The Safari fix means you can safely serve the app over plain HTTP in dev, but you’ll still want HTTPS in production. If you already run Datasette 0.65, the plugin is a drop‑in; older versions will need an upgrade. [FACT:b8b12bf3e952d00649e4fdc7a8767626][FACT:d498f760197187160cd51ea3de3b6be2]
Open Questions

The release is still a single‑source announcement, so we don’t have third‑party benchmark data yet. Open items include: performance impact of the OAuth handshake under high traffic, compatibility with custom authentication backends, and roadmap for supporting other OAuth providers. Builders should watch for follow‑up releases or community reports before committing to large‑scale rollouts. [FACT:95b9f89a81becbb5db4a298c4b9c1042][FACT:c54a37e27696caa08553e2659c8c99d4]
Ardur Take

The plugin fills a measurable gap for Datasette users who need quick, secure login. With version 1.0 stable on GitHub and the Safari bug resolved, it’s worth a trial in a staging environment. Hold off on production‑wide adoption until broader community feedback appears, but plan to incorporate it for any new Datasette service that will be exposed to external users. [FACT:95b9f89a81becbb5db4a298c4b9c1042][FACT:b8b12bf3e952d00649e4fdc7a8767626]
